summary: 1. Key operational findings: 1. 2. Ore collapsed to a 45.6% miss on an all-LG blend (992 BCM vs a 1,822 BCM target) — the steepest single-day ore shortfall of the July run, a sharp reversal from July 13's +347.5% beat, and the first month-to-date narrowing of the ore surplus this run (+34.3%, down from +38.8%). 2. 3. Crusher feed craters to 2,064 BCM, the lowest daily figure of the July dataset, after an 11-hour maintenance stoppage — the largest single crusher downtime entry logged this month. 3. 4. The Drill Rig fleet craters to 69.27% daily availability, a 15.73-point MTD swing and the largest single-fleet variance in the July dataset — two new drifter faults (DR-125, DR-303) land the same day as the standing DR-343 overhaul, and drilling itself misses target for the first time since July 12. 5. EX-123 stays down a ninth straight day (since July 6), DT-108 a second day, DZ-249 a seventh day, and GS-323 a 15th day — four standing faults now all running multi-day to multi-week. 6. Equipment running hours: dump-truck hours and diesel fell together for the first time in several days (369.9 hrs / 27,652 L), breaking the worsening liters-per-hour trend flagged since July 12 — worth watching whether it holds or was a one-off low-activity day. 7. HSEQ escalates the tire/suspension cost pattern by email, sent 05:20 AM the morning after the July 14 meeting first quantified it at 600,000 SAR over two months — names road condition and operator behavior as leading factors and pictures DT-244, DT-128, DT-283, and DT-366 as recent damage examples. 8. The July 14 water-usage row reads identical to the KB's previously logged June 6 record high (19 trips / 307,800 L) — worth a direct check against the site's own water-truck log before treating July 14 as a genuine second record-equalling day. 9. Grade Control picked up new July 14 entries across several block grids, continuing the standing block-grid reconciliation gap open since the 45th pass. A Quarterly Production Inspection report, checklist, and cover email landed in Safety Report — out of scope for this dashboard-scoped pass, registered at index level only, findings not summarized here. An Important References email containing a named production-department employee's personal medical/fitness-for-duty correspondence landed. Held for the next full-scope compile out of respect for employee privacy — not analyzed, summarized, or actioned this pass. No new INX-SUM survey file has landed for Day 20 (would reconcile July 14's truck count); [[survey-volume-reconciliation]] untouched this pass, its MTD gap headline still reflecting Day 19's +4.37%. Wiki updates: [[daily-production-report]] (new July 14 section — production/ore/waste variance, crusher feed and downtime, drilling, machinery, cross-source checks; `Sources` frontmatter) and [[fleet-availability-utilization]] (new July 14 Daily Availability Final Report table and fleet breakdown, Equipment running hours Jul-(14) subsection, Tire Damages escalation email note; `Sources` frontmatter) — both `Last updated` bumped to 2026-07-15 (62nd pass); `Wiki/INDEX.md` one-line descriptions refreshed for both. Full detail in `RAW/_INGESTED.md` under "62nd compile pass." ---
